angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 439,682 km at 124.46 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.0345 +/- 0.0163 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 124.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.632 +/- 0.063 solar radii from Hirano et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-148 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract): 439,682 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.65 +/- 0.061 solar masses from Hirano et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-148 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4079 +/- 70 K from Hirano et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-148 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hirano et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-148 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-148.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.650, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
